-------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m1p2t2 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Total
VARIABLES free, usedA, usedB, holder

TypeOK == /\ free \in 0..Total
          /\ usedA \in 0..Total
          /\ usedB \in 0..Total
          /\ holder \in {"A", "B"}

Init == /\ free = Total
        /\ usedA = 0
        /\ usedB = 0
        /\ holder = "A"

AllocA == /\ holder = "A"
          /\ free > 0
          /\ usedA' = usedA + 1
          /\ free' = free - 1
          /\ UNCHANGED <<usedB, holder>>

AllocB == /\ holder = "B"
          /\ free > 0
          /\ usedB' = usedB + 1
          /\ free' = free - 1
          /\ UNCHANGED <<usedA, holder>>

RelA == /\ usedA > 0
        /\ usedA' = usedA - 1
        /\ free' = free + 1
        /\ UNCHANGED <<usedB, holder>>

RelB == /\ usedB > 0
        /\ usedB' = usedB - 1
        /\ free' = free + 1
        /\ UNCHANGED <<usedA, holder>>

PassToken == /\ holder' = (IF holder = "A" THEN "B" ELSE "A")
             /\ UNCHANGED <<free, usedA, usedB>>

Next == AllocA \/ AllocB \/ RelA \/ RelB \/ PassToken

Vars == <<free, usedA, usedB, holder>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

RoomConservation == free + usedA + usedB = Total
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Total = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT RoomConservation
nl:
Two independent surgery-scheduling instances, Alpha and Beta, cooperate to hand out operating rooms drawn from one shared pool at a hospital. A single grant token circulates on a ring between the two instances, and only the instance currently holding the token is permitted to allocate or release a room, which guarantees exclusive access to the pool. Each room is either free, in use by Alpha, or in use by Beta, and no room is ever conjured up or discarded. Alpha may claim a free room while holding the token, incrementing its own in-use count and decrementing the free count. Either instance may release a room it holds, returning it to the free pool. When an instance is done acting it may pass the token to the other instance around the ring. The hospital audits the books by summing free rooms and rooms in use by each instance. That total must always equal the fixed size of the room pool.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of free rooms plus the rooms in use by Alpha plus the rooms in use by Beta always equals the fixed total number of rooms in the pool.

CONSTANT MaxCap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
A regional network restocks a vending machine through a two-phase commit run by a central coordinator against the machine as participant. Restocking a can proceeds only after a prepare phase in which the participant agrees, followed by a commit that actually deposits the can. The machine has a capacity that facilities staff may raise or lower at runtime, but they may never lower it below the number of cans currently loaded. A commit that would push the loaded count above the current capacity is not allowed to fire. Customers may dispense a can at any time, reducing the loaded count. The coordinator tracks a phase that is either idle or prepared. The auditors care that the machine is never overfilled beyond whatever its capacity happens to be at that moment.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cans loaded in the machine never exceeds the machine's current capacity.

              /\ UNCHANGED <<lo, leader>>

\* A slow follower's confirmation records a past watermark of the shared record

Failover == leader' = (IF leader = "d1" THEN "d2" ELSE "d1")

NoLostUpdate == lo <= record
=====================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANT MaxRead = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A swarm of wildfire surveillance drones keeps a single shared record of the highest fire-intensity reading seen so far. One drone at a time is the elected leader and is the only node allowed to write the shared record; if the leader is deemed unreachable a failover promotes another drone to leader. A drone that is merely slow is not failed: its buffered reading is retained and eventually folded into the record rather than dropped. When the leader commits a reading it takes the maximum of the current record and the incoming reading, so a larger reading is never overwritten by a smaller one. Followers accumulate a pending reading that failover carries forward. The mission demands that no genuinely larger reading is ever lost from the shared record once it has been observed by the swarm.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared record's stored intensity is always at least as large as every reading that has been folded in, so a larger observed reading is never lost.

DispatchAtMostOnce == dispatched <= 1
=====================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Nodes = {"A", "B"}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispatchAtMostOnce
nl:
An airport baggage router decides which chute a bag goes down, and dropping a bag down a chute is irreversible. Competing sorter nodes race to claim the bag by attempting a compare-and-swap on a single ownership register that starts empty; only a swap that observes the register still empty succeeds in claiming ownership. Because claim messages can be reordered on the network, a late claim may arrive after ownership is already set, but the compare-and-swap makes that late claim a no-op. Once some node owns the bag, exactly that ownership entitles the one-time dispatch down the chute. The router counts how many times the bag has been physically dispatched. No matter how claims interleave or reorder, the bag must go down a chute at most once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The bag is physically dispatched down a chute at most one time.

UnitConservation == main + ward = Total
=====================================================================

CONSTANTS Total = 2
          MaxCap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT UnitConservation
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker moves units between a main fridge and a ward fridge using a two-phase commit. A transfer of one unit is first prepared, then committed, at which point one unit leaves the main fridge and appears in the ward fridge; an abort cancels the prepared transfer. Units are never created or destroyed, only relocated, so the combined holdings of the two fridges is fixed. The ward fridge has a capacity that maintenance can raise or lower at runtime, but never below what it currently holds, and a transfer only prepares if the ward has room. A coordinator phase is either idle or prepared. Auditors require that the total number of blood units across both fridges stays constant no matter how transfers and capacity changes interleave.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The sum of blood units in the main fridge and the ward fridge always equals the fixed total.

NoUnauthorizedCommit == committed => (votes >= Quorum \/ adminOn)
=====================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Staff = 3
          Quorum = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoUnauthorizedCommit
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker only enacts a withdrawal after the change is authorized. Under normal operation, staff cast votes and a withdrawal may commit only once a quorum of votes has been gathered, so no unauthorized or stale participant can push a change through on its own. A privileged administrator can flip an override that authorizes a commit even without a quorum, for emergencies. Votes accumulate for the pending withdrawal and are frozen at the moment of commit so the authorizing evidence cannot be rewritten afterward. Once a withdrawal is committed it stands. The compliance rule is that any committed withdrawal was backed either by a genuine quorum of votes or by the administrator's override.
SAFETY PROPERTY: If a withdrawal has been committed, then at commit it was backed by at least a quorum of votes or by the administrator override.

A subway signalling system manages a shared pool of track blocks between two independent control instances that both draw from the same pool. A car-wash conveyor line holds cars between the entry gate and the exit. The line runs in numbered epochs, and a reconfiguration advances to the next epoch while resetting the line's capacity to a new value chosen for that epoch. Cars enter at the gate while there is room and leave at the exit. Thus the line's capacity genuinely changes at runtime across epochs. The operator's hard limit is that the number of cars on the conveyor never exceeds the capacity in force for the current epoch.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cars on the conveyor never exceeds the current epoch's capacity.

nl:
A library book reservation system tracks copies of a popular title split between an available shelf and a reserved-hold count, with two independent branch instances drawing on the same shared pool of copies. A patron's reservation is approved only after branch librarians cast votes and a quorum is reached, at which point one copy moves from available to reserved and the vote tally resets. Returning a held copy moves it back from reserved to available. Copies are never printed or shredded in this system, only moved between the two buckets, so the grand total of copies is fixed. The catalog integrity rule is that available copies plus reserved copies always equals the fixed total number of copies of that title.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of available copies plus the number of reserved copies always equals the fixed total number of copies.

          MaxCap = 3

nl:
A car-wash conveyor line is reconfigured in numbered epochs, and each control command carries the epoch number under which it was submitted. When a command is submitted it is stamped with the current epoch and enters a prepared state; committing the command actually reconfigures the line's capacity. A reconfiguration advances the epoch, which makes any command stamped with an older epoch stale, so a prepared command left over from a previous epoch is invalidated rather than applied. Only a command whose stamp matches the current epoch is authorized to commit. The controller keeps at most one command in flight, either idle or prepared. The safety rule the operators insist on is that any command sitting prepared and about to act carries the current epoch, so no stale participant's leftover command can slip through.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a command is in the prepared state, its stamped epoch equals the current epoch.

BoundedUnlocked == unlocked <= allowance
=====================================================================

CONSTANTS MaxCap = 2
          MaxVer = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BoundedUnlocked
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network limits how many doors may be simultaneously unlocked to a configurable allowance. Each unlock uses optimistic locking against a shared version counter: a controller reads the version, and its unlock only takes effect if the version has not changed since the read, otherwise the controller retries. Every successful unlock or relock bumps the version. The homeowner may raise or lower the allowance at runtime, but may never lower it below the number of doors currently unlocked. Stale writers whose expected version no longer matches simply retry and change nothing. The security guarantee is that the number of doors unlocked at once never exceeds the current allowance.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of simultaneously unlocked doors never exceeds the current allowance.

spec_text:
------------------------ MODULE W4Od4m9p3t3 ------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Slots, Cars, MaxEpoch
VARIABLES assign, epoch

Init == assign = [s \in Slots |-> "none"] /\ epoch = 0

Assign(s, c) == assign[s] = "none"
                /\ (\A t \in Slots : assign[t] # c)
                /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![s] = c]
                /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Release(s) == assign[s] # "none"
              /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
              /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Reconfigure == epoch < MaxEpoch /\ epoch' = epoch + 1 /\ UNCHANGED assign

Next == (\E s \in Slots, c \in Cars : Assign(s, c))
        \/ (\E s \in Slots : Release(s))
        \/ Reconfigure
vars == <<assign, epoch>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A s1, s2 \in Slots :
     (s1 # s2 /\ assign[s1] # "none") => assign[s1] # assign[s2]
=====================================================================
nl:
A car-wash conveyor assigns each arriving car to a wash bay slot. The yard is reconfigured in numbered epochs, but a reconfiguration only advances the epoch counter and never evicts a car that already holds a slot, because a car that is merely slow to finish is not treated as gone. A car may be assigned to a free slot only if it does not already occupy some other slot, and a finished car releases its slot. Because each car holds at most one slot and each slot holds at most one car, the same car is never allocated to two different slots at once. The operators require that no car is double-allocated: two distinct occupied slots never name the same car.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct occupied slots are ever assigned to the same car.

Normally the match may launch only after at least one rebalancing epoch has completed so teams are fair, but a privileged administrator can flip an override that permits an immediate launch regardless of epoch. The system counts how many times a match has been launched from this lobby. The integrity requirement is that a match is launched at most one time.

NoUnauthorizedServe == served <= reg
=====================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANT MaxVer = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoUnauthorizedServe
nl:
A library book reservation system serializes holds on a hot title through a single compare-and-swap register that acts as a version counter. A patron's client first reads the register to stamp its pending request, then serves the hold only if the register still matches the stamp, atomically bumping the register as it serves. Concurrent writers may bump the register in between, and because requests can be reordered on the wire, a request that was stamped earlier can find the register already advanced and must back off rather than serve. Every genuine serve consumes exactly one advance of the register. The consistency rule is that the number of holds actually served never runs ahead of the register's value, so no stale or unauthorized client can serve a hold out of turn.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of holds served never exceeds the compare-and-swap register's value.

LeasesWithinCapacity == active <= Capacity
=====================================================================

          MaxClock = 3

nl:
A container-ship crane yard grants cranes short leases on stacking slots. At most a fixed number of leases may be active at once, the yard's working capacity. A crane acquires a lease while capacity remains, and a lease is released only when it expires as the yard clock advances; a crane that is merely slow to finish keeps its lease until expiry and is never forcibly evicted. The yard clock ticks forward over a bounded shift. Because leases are released only through expiry and never yanked away, and new leases are refused once capacity is reached, the number of active leases stays within the working capacity. The operational safety rule is that the number of active slot leases never exceeds the yard's working capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of active slot leases never exceeds the yard's fixed working capacity.

CONSTANTS Total = 2
          MaxVer = 3
INIT Init

nl:
A power-grid load shedder holds a fixed number of load units that are each either currently served or currently shed. Rebalancing moves one unit between served and shed using optimistic concurrency: a controller reads a version counter, computes the move, and applies it only if the version is unchanged, bumping the version on success. Because control messages can be reordered, a controller that acted on a stale version simply retries and changes nothing. No load unit is ever created or destroyed; units only migrate between the served and shed buckets. Thus the sum of served and shed units is fixed at the grid's total load. The dispatch invariant is that served units plus shed units always equals the fixed total number of load units.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of served load units plus the number of shed load units always equals the fixed total load.

           /\ queue' = queue + 1 /\ accepted' = accepted + 1 /\ UNCHANGED record

           /\ UNCHANGED accepted

NoLostUpdate == record + queue = accepted
=====================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS MaxQueue = 2
          MaxAccepted = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A library book reservation system funnels incoming reservation requests through a bounded work queue before they are written to the shared reservation record. When the queue is full, backpressure refuses new requests rather than dropping them silently, so a request is only accepted if there is room to enqueue it. Each accepted request waits in the queue and is later processed exactly once, writing one entry into the shared record. Requests may be processed in any order because they can be reordered, but every accepted request is eventually either still waiting in the queue or already written to the record, never lost. The durability guarantee is that the number of records written plus the number still queued equals the number of requests accepted, so no accepted update is ever lost.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of records written to the shared record plus the number of requests still in the queue always equals the number of requests accepted.

spec_text:
------------------------ MODULE W4Od18m6p5t5 ------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES resetCount, holder, adminOn

Init == resetCount = 0 /\ holder = "none" /\ adminOn = FALSE

Acquire == holder = "none" /\ holder' = "ctrl" /\ UNCHANGED <<resetCount, adminOn>>

Expire == holder = "ctrl" /\ holder' = "none" /\ UNCHANGED <<resetCount, adminOn>>

ToggleAdmin == adminOn' = ~adminOn /\ UNCHANGED <<resetCount, holder>>

FactoryReset == resetCount = 0 /\ (holder = "ctrl" \/ adminOn)
                /\ resetCount' = resetCount + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, adminOn>>

Next == Acquire \/ Expire \/ ToggleAdmin \/ FactoryReset
vars == <<resetCount, holder, adminOn>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ResetAtMostOnce == resetCount <= 1
=====================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ResetAtMostOnce
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network protects one irreversible operation: a factory reset that wipes all credentials, which may happen at most once. Control of the lock is granted by a lease: at most one controller holds the lease at a time, acquiring it when free and losing it when the lease expires. Only the current lease holder may trigger the factory reset, except that a privileged administrator can flip an override that authorizes the reset even without holding the lease. The system counts how many factory resets have occurred. Once the reset fires it stands and cannot be undone. The safety rule is that the factory reset is performed at most one time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The factory reset is performed at most one time.

------------------------ MODULE W4Od9m5p1t0 ------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Agents, AgentsAfterCrash, Quorum, MaxSubmitted
VARIABLES record, submitted, votes, crashed

Init == record = 0 /\ submitted = 0 /\ votes = 0 /\ crashed = FALSE

Submit == submitted < MaxSubmitted /\ submitted' = submitted + 1
          /\ UNCHANGED <<record, votes, crashed>>

Vote == votes < (IF crashed THEN AgentsAfterCrash ELSE Agents)
        /\ votes' = votes + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<record, submitted, crashed>>

Commit == submitted - record > 0 /\ votes >= Quorum
          /\ record' = record + 1 /\ votes' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<submitted, crashed>>

Crash == ~crashed /\ crashed' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED <<record, submitted, votes>>

Idle == UNCHANGED <<record, submitted, votes, crashed>>

Next == Submit \/ Vote \/ Commit \/ Crash \/ Idle
vars == <<record, submitted, votes, crashed>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate == record <= submitted

CONSTANTS Agents = 3
          AgentsAfterCrash = 2
          Quorum = 2
          MaxSubmitted = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A power-grid load shedder writes shed decisions into a shared record only after a quorum of relay agents votes to approve the pending decision. Decisions are submitted into a backlog and each committed decision writes one entry to the shared record, with the vote tally reset after a commit. One relay agent may crash silently, after which it no longer contributes votes, but the remaining agents can still form a quorum. No submitted decision is dropped: every decision that was submitted is either still awaiting its quorum in the backlog or already written to the record. The durability rule is that the number of decisions written to the shared record never exceeds the number of decisions submitted, so no update is fabricated or lost.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of decisions written to the shared record never exceeds the number of decisions submitted.

nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler locks in the start of a surgery, an irreversible commitment that must occur at most once for a given case. Two independent scheduler instances share the one case and either may be the one acting, with control passing back and forth between them. The schedule is reconfigured in numbered epochs as staffing is finalized, and a surgery start is only permitted once at least one reconfiguration epoch has completed. The system counts how many times the surgery has been started. Whichever instance acts, and however epochs advance, the surgery must be started at most one time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The surgery is started at most one time.

CONSTANT MaxCap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler guards one sterile operating table that only a single surgery may occupy at a time. Two surgical teams contend for the table through a compare-and-swap lock register that starts empty: a team acquires the table only if the lock is observed free, atomically writing its identity, and releases it by clearing the lock. Separately, the overall room capacity of the wing is adjusted at runtime as rooms open and close, but that never affects the single-occupancy rule for this one table. The absolute safety rule is that the two teams are never both operating on the sterile table at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The two surgical teams are never both in the operating (critical) section on the sterile table simultaneously.

INIT Init

nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm shares one directional water-drop nozzle that only a single drone may control at any instant. Drones contend for control using optimistic locking against a shared lock: a drone reads the lock, and its acquire takes effect only if the lock is still free, otherwise it backs off and retries. The controlling drone releases the nozzle when done. A privileged mission administrator can flip an override that forcibly resets the nozzle control, clearing whoever holds it, for safety. Optimistic retries and administrator resets may interleave freely. The hard constraint is that two drones are never both in control of the nozzle at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Two drones are never both in the controlling (critical) section of the nozzle at the same time.

nl:
A smart-home door-lock network journals configuration updates into a shared record, one entry per applied update. Updates first land in a bounded staging buffer, and a compare-and-swap on the record applies exactly one staged update at a time, never losing or duplicating a staged entry. The staging buffer's capacity is adjusted at runtime, but is never lowered below the number of updates currently staged. An update may be submitted into staging only while there is buffer room. Every submitted update is either still staged or already applied to the record. The durability guarantee is that the number of updates applied to the shared record never exceeds the number of updates submitted, so no update is ever lost.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of updates applied to the shared record never exceeds the number of updates submitted.

------------------------ MODULE W4Od1m1p3t1 ------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Slots
VARIABLES grants, holder

Init == grants = [s \in Slots |-> 0] /\ holder = "A"

GrantA(s) == holder = "A" /\ grants[s] = 0
             /\ grants' = [grants EXCEPT ![s] = grants[s] + 1] /\ UNCHANGED holder
GrantB(s) == holder = "B" /\ grants[s] = 0
             /\ grants' = [grants EXCEPT ![s] = grants[s] + 1] /\ UNCHANGED holder

Land(s) == grants[s] = 1 /\ grants' = [grants EXCEPT ![s] = 0] /\ UNCHANGED holder

PassToken == holder' = (IF holder = "A" THEN "B" ELSE "A") /\ UNCHANGED grants

Next == (\E s \in Slots : GrantA(s) \/ GrantB(s) \/ Land(s)) \/ PassToken
vars == <<grants, holder>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation == \A s \in Slots : grants[s] <= 1

CONSTANT Slots = {"r1", "r2"}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator hands out runway slots to inbound flights. A single grant token circulates on a ring between two allocator instances, and only the instance currently holding the token may grant a slot. Granting a slot marks it allocated; the same slot may only be granted when it is currently free, and a landing clears the slot back to free. Because grant messages can be reordered, an instance that does not hold the token may see a stale grant attempt, which the token discipline turns into a no-op. Each slot therefore carries an allocation count that must never rise above one. The controller's safety rule is that no runway slot is ever double-allocated: each slot's allocation count stays at most one.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No runway slot is allocated more than once at a time; each slot's allocation count never exceeds one.

ReleaseA == stateA = "active" /\ stateA' = "idle" /\ UNCHANGED <<stateB, cap>>

CommitB == stateB = "prepared" /\ stateA # "active" /\ stateB' = "active"
           /\ UNCHANGED <<stateA, cap>>
AbortB == stateB = "prepared" /\ stateB' = "idle" /\ UNCHANGED <<stateA, cap>>
ReleaseB == stateB = "active" /\ stateB' = "idle" /\ UNCHANGED <<stateA, cap>>

ChangeCap == \E c \in 1..MaxCap : cap' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<stateA, stateB>>

Next == PrepareA \/ CommitA \/ AbortA \/ ReleaseA
        \/ PrepareB \/ CommitB \/ AbortB \/ ReleaseB \/ ChangeCap

CONSTANT MaxCap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BreakerMutualExclusion
nl:
A power-grid load shedder controls one critical breaker that only a single shed transaction may drive at a time. Two dispatch participants each run a two-phase commit to take the breaker: a participant first prepares, then commits into the active driving state, but a commit into active is only permitted when the other participant is not currently active. Either participant may abort a prepared transaction, and an active participant releases the breaker when finished. Separately, the amount of sheddable capacity is reconfigured at runtime as demand shifts, independent of who drives the breaker. The overriding safety rule is that the two participants are never both actively driving the breaker at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The two dispatch participants are never both in the active breaker-driving state at the same time.
